hypotheses.text: The limb phenotype in Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome (STISS) is restricted to preaxial or mild distal digital anomalies (such as hypoplastic thumbs, preaxial polydactyly, brachydactyly, or syndactyly) in roughly 15-35% of individuals, whereas severe longitudinal or transverse terminal limb reduction defects (e.g., phocomelia, ectrodactyly, or oligodactyly typical of Cornelia de Lange or Holt-Oram syndromes) are absent and serve as an exclusion criterion.
hypotheses.rationale: Extends the confirmed prior regarding exclusionary limb defects by delineating the positive limb spectrum in PSMD12 haploinsufficiency (preaxial hand abnormalities) from severe reduction malformations.

evidence.text: In an expanded cohort of 24 unrelated patients with STISS, preaxial hand abnormalities were confirmed as a recurrent feature, whereas terminal longitudinal limb reduction or severe anterior limb absence was not observed.

source.title: Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome: expanding the clinical and molecular phenotype
source.quote: In addition to previously reported DD/ID, speech delay, cardiac and renal anomalies, we also confirmed preaxial hand abnormalities as a feature of this syndrome.

evidence.text: The original delineation of PSMD12 haploinsufficiency identified congenital malformations including minor digital and craniofacial anomalies without severe terminal reduction defects.

source.title: Interpretable Clinical Genomics with a Likelihood Ratio ...
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: we identified six de novo genomic deletions and four de novo point mutations involving PSMD12, encoding the non-ATPase subunit PSMD12... in unrelated individuals with intellectual disability, congenital malformations, ophthalmologic anomalies, feeding difficulties, deafness, and subtle dysmorphic facial features.

hypotheses.text: Cutaneous interferonopathy-like features (specifically chilblains/pernio-like lesions) occur in a distinct minority (~8-10%) of STISS patients; while their absence cannot exclude STISS, their presence discriminates STISS from phenotypically overlapping non-proteasomal neurodevelopmental syndromes like Cornelia de Lange or Rubinstein-Taybi.
hypotheses.rationale: Clarifies the diagnostic utility of cutaneous autoinflammatory features: they are not sufficiently penetrant to be required for diagnosis, but their presence provides high positive discriminative value among neurodevelopmental disorders.

evidence.text: Across an expanded cohort of 24 individuals with PSMD12 mutations, exactly 2 individuals manifested chilblains, corresponding to a subclinical or low-penetrance interferonopathy phenotype.

source.title: Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome: expanding the clinical and molecular phenotype
source.quote: Of note, 2 patients also showed chilblains resembling signs observed in interferonopathy. Remarkably, our data show that STISS patient cells exhibit a profound remodeling of the mTORC1 and mitophagy pathways with an induction of type I interferon-stimulated genes.

evidence.text: Proteasome-associated neurodevelopmental disorders exhibit type I interferon signaling upregulation, though classic severe systemic autoinflammation remains secondary or restricted compared to proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndromes.

source.title: Molecular mechanisms in rare proteasomopathies - PMC - NIH
source.quote: Two distinct clinical phenotypes have been characterised in proteasomopathies so far: (i) proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndromes and (ii) proteasome-associated neurodevelopmental disorders. Despite these differences, both syndromes show molecular similarities with protein aggregation, activated stress responses, metabolic imbalance and dysregulated type I interferon signalling.

hypotheses.text: Isolated fetal horseshoe kidney represents an ultra-rare presentation of PSMD12 variants (prevalence ~1-2% among isolated fetal horseshoe kidney cases), and postnatally these individuals invariably manifest neurodevelopmental delay or subtle craniofacial dysmorphism rather than maintaining truly isolated renal disease.
hypotheses.rationale: Evaluates whether isolated congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract can be an isolated lifelong manifestation of PSMD12 haploinsufficiency or if syndromic developmental delay will manifest upon longitudinal assessment.

evidence.text: In a series of 95 fetuses with isolated horseshoe kidney, exome sequencing among CMA-negative cases identified a pathogenic splicing variant in PSMD12 (c.796-1G>A) in exactly 1 of 45 cases (2.2% of sequenced, 1.1% of entire cohort).

source.title: Clinically Significant Genetic Results in Fetuses With Isolated Horseshoe Kidney
source.quote: Among the cases that yielded negative results from CMA, 45 proceeded to trio ES. Notably, two disease-causing variants, c.796-1G > A in PSMD12 and c.11707 C > T (p.Gln3903*) in KMT2D, were detected in each case.

new_directions.question_text: What is the long-term neurodevelopmental outcome of prenatal fetuses diagnosed with PSMD12 variants presenting with isolated horseshoe kidney?
new_directions.rationale: Determine whether PSMD12 haploinsufficiency can ever result in non-syndromic isolated renal malformations or if subclinical developmental delay and dysmorphism always appear postnatally.

new_directions.question_text: Does the presence of elevated blood type I interferon gene expression score discriminate PSMD12-related STISS from other neurodevelopmental syndromes presenting with preaxial limb anomalies and microcephaly?
new_directions.rationale: Establish whether interferonopathy blood biomarker profiling can serve as an accessible clinical test before or alongside exome sequencing.
